reviewer: Codex visual inspection of saved PNGs and real Chromium captures
scope: Static two-head SD field example; artistic judgment separate from technical reports
observations: Large heads and short limbs replace the previous tall character proportions. All three keep the frozen 48x96 canvas.

Eyes and small mouths are separated on the native faces. The knight's helmet, sword and shield; the princess's crown, hair and dress; and the demon king's horns and armor remain distinguishable in the composed field.

All three share the y=92 foot baseline. Visible heights are 65, 69 and 63 pixels; the crown and plume explain some silhouette differences. The boss uses more canvas width to keep its face comparable in size.
Each character has one 8-connected alpha component. No detached opaque speck like the old boss is present; this is supporting evidence, not an automatic aesthetic score.
Upper-left highlights, dark stepped contours, gold/crimson accents and cool shadows connect the independently generated characters and new castle.
Four stone and four sparse moss variants vary the ground. A separate binary-alpha shadow anchors each character to the paving without introducing blended colors.
The normal field contains no checker highlights. Failure overlays are separate, explicitly labeled evidence.
limitations: Fine source shading and some eye highlights are simplified by the recorded projection and palette mapping; raw-generation acceptance is not claimed.
This review covers static readability and composition. The moving object uses a fixed pose and has no walk cycle.
reason: User review identified damaged expressions. Prior art approval withdrawn; technical grid compliance did not establish expression fidelity.
